data.text:
Malaysia works ~2,308 hours a year.
Germany works ~1,386.
that's basically an extra 25 work weeks.
and yet somehow Germany has a higher average monthly salary than us.
something doesn't add up.

here's the full picture on annual working hours across SEA:
•⁠  Cambodia: ~2,389 
•⁠  Malaysia: ~2,308 
•⁠  Singapore: ~2,283 
•⁠  Thailand: ~2,177 
•⁠  Vietnam: ~2,160 
•⁠  Philippines: ~2,096 
•⁠  ⁠⁠Indonesia: ~2,020
•⁠  Germany: ~1,386
we outworked the countries we were supposed to catch up to.
(source: ILO via Our World in Data, 2023)

and the painful part:
the countries working the longest hours often earn the least.
•⁠  ⁠⁠Singapore: ~$4,350/month 
•⁠  ⁠⁠Germany: ~$4,200/month 
•⁠  ⁠⁠Malaysia: ~$855/month 
•⁠  ⁠⁠Thailand: ~$508/month 
•⁠  ⁠⁠Vietnam: ~$448/month 
•⁠  ⁠⁠Indonesia: ~$344/month 
•⁠  ⁠⁠Cambodia: ~$215/month
apparently being exhausted is not a high-income skill.
(source: Picodi 2024 Global Net Salary Report)

the global economy doesn't reward hours.
it rewards leverage. technology. capital. high-value industries.
•⁠  ⁠⁠not "I skipped lunch and cried in Google sheets."
•⁠  ⁠⁠not "I replied to 200 Telegram messages before 9am."
•⁠  ⁠⁠not "I shipped 6 bounties last week on zero sleep."
the hours are real. the reward structure is broken.

this explains so much about growing up in SEA.
•⁠  ⁠⁠why everyone runs on kopi-o and teh tarik.
•⁠  ⁠⁠why everyone has back or knee pain before 30.
•⁠  ⁠⁠why your parents answer work calls at family dinners.
•⁠  ⁠⁠why remote work somehow became "always available, including CNY eve."
we were born into this hustle culture.

and our parents were grinding long before it became a LinkedIn post.
they had the mindset of: "don't waste the opportunities we never had."
that one sentence sent an entire generation into overwork without questioning whether more hours was actually the answer.

but here's where it gets interesting for builders in CT right now.
AI is supposed to change this equation.
if the old bottleneck was hours, and AI compresses the hours required to produce - then SEA's work ethic compounding with AI leverage should be genuinely unstoppable.
and for a moment, that felt like the obvious take.

but there's a catch worth sitting with:
AI democratised code - now there are more dApps, more projects, more hackathon submissions than ever. that's the good part.
but it's also flooding social media, email, and identity verification with increasingly convincing spam and slop.
and security is a real concern. when anyone can ship code without understanding the fundamentals, the attack surface grows. you can vibe-code a product but you can't vibe-code your way out of a hack (...yet😅).

the real edge going forward won't be who works the most hours.
it'll be who knows you. who vouches for you. who you've shipped with before.
AI can't fake that.

this is why communities like @SuperteamMY and @ns matter more, not less, as AI scales.

we have the work ethic already hardwired. time to compound it with real trust.
bullish on the builders who figure this out first.
